chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Early sideman records: Big Joe Turner, Sister Rosetta Tharpe, Sugar Charles
summary: He recorded with Joe Turner, for Decca with Rosetta Tharpe, and with Sugar Charles around 1944, a date he forgot but a fan in Germany remembered.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Tell me about some of your recordings, your own. When was your first recording?
Well, the first recording -- I can't remember when the first -- I made --

Well, as a sideman I made records with -- oh, I made -- we would go in the studio, like, with Big Joe Turner, and we would just play until he passed out. We'd make records. And then I made a lot of records for Decca, with Rosetta Tharpe.
Sister Rosetta Tharpe. And then when I was in Germany a kid came up to me and was asking me about records I made with Sugar Charles. Do you remember him?
He was from Detroit, wasn't he?
Right, from Detroit. And this guy remembered who we had on bass and he remembered everything. I didn't even remember the tunes.
This gig really escaped my mind, you know?
It was right around in there, right, right.
